capabilities.justification: The command line reads the files the caller names with --warrant (a .warrant specification), --profile (corpus.profile) and optionally --bindings (an evidence.bindings file), and --check reads back the generated files of the caller-named --out directory. Every read goes through fsio::read_regular: only a regular file is opened (a FIFO or directory is refused, never opened), through a handle, and never more than the cap (4 MiB for an input, the expected length plus one byte for a generated file), so a hostile path cannot hang or exhaust the tool. generate() itself performs no I/O.

fsio.rs lists the chunks/ directory of the caller-named --out directory so write mode can refuse (never delete) a file the corpus does not own and --check can report one (names are escaped before they are printed), and it stats paths with symlink_metadata to refuse a symbolic link present at chunks/ or at a target, and to refuse an input that is not a regular file.

Write mode creates the caller-named --out directory and its chunks/ subdirectory if missing (create_dir_all), after every file path has been validated against fsio::guard (corpus.json, cases.tfv or chunks/<plain name>.txt) and before anything is written.

Write mode writes only the files of the generated corpus (corpus.json, cases.tfv, chunks/<claim>.txt) below the caller-named --out directory. Each goes to a reserved temporary name (.<name>.tmp) created with create_new (O_EXCL: it never follows a link, reuses an inode or opens a FIFO) and is renamed into place, corpus.json last. fsio::guard refuses every other path (no separator beyond chunks/, no .., no leading dot, no absolute path); a symbolic link present at chunks/ or at a target is refused. Concurrent modification of the output directory by another process is not defended against.

The only deletions are of the generator's own reserved temporary file (.<name>.tmp in the directory of the file being written): a leftover or planted entry at that name is unlinked (a hard link is unlinked, never written through) before the exclusive create, and the temporary is removed after a failed write. The generator never deletes any other file; a foreign file in chunks/ makes write mode refuse.
src/bin/warrant-corpus-gen.rs reads its command-line arguments (--warrant, --profile, --out, --check, --bindings). No environment variable is read.

src/bin/warrant-corpus-gen.rs calls std::process::exit(status) after cli::run has returned, only to give the process the status 2 (refused) or 1 (--check drift): a status other than 0 or 1 cannot be returned from main without std::process. It signals no other process, spawns nothing and passes no argument to a program.
The CLI reports success on standard output and a refusal, a note or a drift (file, line, column, byte offset; never file content, and foreign file names escaped) on standard error.

justification: The generator proper (lowering, evaluation, enumeration, faults, emission into Strings) is pure in-memory computation. File access exists only to read the inputs the command line names, to write the generated fixture directory below the output directory the caller names (guarded by a name whitelist, symlink refusal at start and O_EXCL temporaries; concurrent modification unsupported), and to compare an existing directory with the regenerated one (--check). It opens no socket, spawns no process and reads no environment variable. The tests do their file work in temporary directories and embed the specifications with include_str!.
